name: Antonov An-32 (RE)

what_it_is.prose: The Antonov An-32 is a Ukraine-origin (ex-Soviet) twin-turboprop medium transport that has been the Indian Air Force's tactical-airlift workhorse since induction began in 1984. The IAF operates roughly 100 or more airframes, prized for 'hot-and-high' performance from Himalayan Advanced Landing Grounds in Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh, and used for troop and cargo transport, para-drop, medical evacuation and HADR. The aircraft is powered by two Ivchenko-Progress AI-20D turboprops and carries about 6.7–7.5 tonnes or up to 50 troops. To modernise the ageing fleet, India signed a roughly $400 million upgrade contract with Antonov of Ukraine in 2009 to bring aircraft to the 'An-32RE' standard — new avionics, navigation, refurbished airframes and improved cockpit — with about 40 aircraft overhauled in Ukraine and a further ~64 at the IAF's No. 1 Base Repair Depot (BRD) in Kanpur under transfer of technology. The programme faltered after 2014–15 as Russia's annexation of Crimea and the wider Russia-Ukraine conflict disrupted the supply chain from Ukraine; only the first tranche of RE aircraft was completed. India has since shifted toward an indigenous overhaul and life-extension route — structural refurbishment, AI-20 engine overhauls, digital avionics/GPS and indigenous spares — carried out by Kanpur BRD together with private Indian firms, aiming to keep at least ~60 airframes flying toward 2040 amid persistent serviceability challenges (a 2017 CAG report cited availability around 40%). The fleet has also suffered several fatal crashes over its service life, keeping replacement (via the Medium Transport Aircraft programme) on the agenda.

deployments_procurement.summary: The IAF inducted the An-32 from 1984 and operates ~100+ aircraft. A $400M Antonov RE upgrade (2009) split between Ukraine and Kanpur BRD stalled after 2014–15 due to the Russia-Ukraine conflict; India now pursues indigenous overhaul and life extension toward 2040, while the fleet remains a candidate for replacement under the MTA programme.

faq.question: How many An-32 does the IAF operate and when were they inducted?
faq.answer: The Indian Air Force operates roughly 100 or more An-32 airframes, its largest medium-transport fleet, with induction beginning in 1984. The Ukraine-origin twin-turboprop is valued for 'hot-and-high' operations from Himalayan Advanced Landing Grounds in Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh.

faq.question: What happened to the An-32 re-engine/upgrade programme?
faq.answer: India signed a roughly $400 million contract with Antonov of Ukraine in 2009 to upgrade aircraft to the 'An-32RE' standard — about 40 in Ukraine and 64 at the IAF's No. 1 Base Repair Depot in Kanpur. The first RE aircraft entered service in 2011, but the programme stalled after 2014–15 when Russia's annexation of Crimea and the Russia-Ukraine war disrupted the Ukrainian supply chain, leaving it incomplete.

faq.question: How will the An-32 fleet be kept in service?
faq.answer: With the OEM route disrupted, the IAF has shifted to an indigenous overhaul and life-extension effort — structural refurbishment, AI-20 engine overhauls, digital avionics/GPS and indigenous spares — run by Kanpur Base Repair Depot with private Indian firms, aiming to keep at least ~60 airframes flying toward 2040, while a longer-term replacement is pursued under the Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) programme.
